chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the Zakat, one may give from it to the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt, and one may not give to the grandfather nor the grandmother.
ai.seo_question: Which relatives are eligible and ineligible to receive Zakat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchy of kinship eligibility for Zakat, prioritizing siblings and aunts/uncles while excluding grandparents, a ruling that reflects the Shia interpretation of 'relatives' (qurba) in the Quranic verse. It highlights the practical application of maintaining family ties (silat al-rahim) through financial support, distinguishing between direct ascendants and collateral relatives. This specific exclusion of grandparents is often discussed in fiqh commentaries to resolve ambiguities regarding the scope of 'close relatives' in Zakat distribution.
